purpose: Test whether a biologically extended Model 3 can reproduce the Chapter 1 island-syndrome pattern in a numerical world, rather than only explain why non-uniformity is possible.

fit_rule.domain_scaling: one nonnegative global least-squares scale per H1 domain; no stratum-specific scale
fit_rule.pollen_limitation_scaling: one positive global scale for H3 because model distance and empirical standardized log-distance units differ
fit_rule.optimization_target: minimize scaled RMSE across the 12 H1 domain slopes plus H3 while requiring positive assurance and accessibility slopes in all four strata
fit_rule.display_mapping: model display_dulling = 1 - mean display-investment trait; this is a proxy and not literal flower colour

held_out_rule.H2: after selecting parameter sets using only H1+H3, fit accessibility ~ isolation + assurance and display_dulling ~ isolation + assurance within each stratum; compare signs and rank pattern with frozen H2
held_out_rule.H4: after selecting parameter sets using only H1+H3, fit pollen_limitation ~ isolation + assurance + accessibility across pseudo-islands; assurance and accessibility coefficients must both be negative to reproduce the held-out functional bridge
held_out_rule.no_retuning: H2/H4 outcomes cannot be used to change parameter-search ranges or acceptance threshold in this first prospective emulation

claim_boundary: Model 3E is an empirical-emulation extension, not the already frozen Model 3.
Display investment is not literal colour; exact regional raw-colour components remain outside direct model calibration.
The first experiment tests whether the domain-level Chapter 1 pattern and held-out functional relations can emerge under one shared biological operator.
A fit does not identify historical causal parameters for named regions.
